Subsequently, 2 days later, she started to experience pain when swallowing and malaise. The examination revealed red pharyngeal mucosa with prominent lymph follicles; the tonsils were red and swollen (Figure 1). There were no palpable enlarged lymph nodes. The patient was subfebrile. Symptoms went away 10 days later without antibiotic treatment. The condition recurred 2 more times during pregnancy. Meanwhile, painless tonsilloliths (tonsil stones) were regularly observed (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Axial contrast-enhanced CT at tonsillar level showing bilateral enlarged tonsils with intraparenchymal gas as described in caption as emphysematous tonsillopharyngitis; swelling maps to tonsillar_erythema_swelling vocabulary, gas has no vocabulary term so proposed. B: Same tonsillar level as A with bilateral tonsillar enlargement and gas locules described as central and submucosal gas locules within palatine tonsillar parenchyma. C: Periepiglottic level showing circumferential inflammatory involvement attributed to same emphysematous tonsillopharyngitis process with significant airway narrowing; inflammatory involvement maps to pharyngeal erythema vocabulary. D: Inferior level showing left-sided laryngocele with gas and inflammatory changes explicitly described as inferior extension of same emphysematous tonsillopharyngitis process; retained as manifestation of target disease extension.

panels.rationale: Axial non-contrast neck CT in a patient with clinical acute tonsillitis; caption and in-text state bulky heterogeneous bilateral palatine tonsils with luminal narrowing and radiologist impression features of tonsillitis. No discrete abscess, so peritonsillar abscess not tagged.
panels.attribution_text: Omer et al. Atypical Presentation of Mpox as Acute Tonsillitis: A Case Report from the United Arab Emirates.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.113748. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: CT of the neck on admission An axial non-contrast CT image at the level of the oropharynx demonstrating bulky, heterogeneous bilateral palatine tonsils with ill-defined hypodense areas and significant narrowing of the oropharyngeal lumen. No discrete abscess is identified. Reactive cervical lymphadenopathy was noted on adjacent slices (not shown). The radiologist’s impression was “features of tonsillitis with the possibility of evolving abscess.”
in_text_mentions: illar abscess. CT of the neck demonstrated bulky, heterogeneous bilateral palatine tonsils with several ill-defined hypodense areas within and significant narrowing of the oropharyngeal lumen (Figure 1). Multiple enlarged cervical lymph nodes were noted, the largest measuring 14 mm at level III. The nasopharynx, epiglottis, aryepiglottic folds, vallecula, pyriform sinuses, vocal cords, laryngeal cartilages, and visualized trachea and esophagus were reported as normal.
